title: Isomorphic Labs breaks biotech VC fundraising record with $5B series C
snippet: After securing $2.1 billion this May, AI-driven drug designer Isomorphic Labs is back with more money—a lot more—securing the industry’s largest private fundraise ever.

title: AstraZeneca, Calidi, Tempest make significant workforce cuts
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: Vertex on the verge of ‘iconic’ evolution as key kidney disease verdict looms
snippet: Analysts are broadly confident that povetacicept will notch an approval in IgA nephropathy by the end of the month, setting up “the next wave” for Vertex Pharmaceuticals.

title: CTAD 2026: AriBio’s Alzheimer’s candidate slows cognitive decline as monotherapy
snippet: At the 2026 Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease conference, AriBio reported that AR1001 slowed cognitive decline more than placebo in patients not taking other drugs for the disease.

title: Sellas’ cancer vaccine slashes death risk by 41% in late-stage AML study
snippet: Sellas Life Sciences’ investigational cancer vaccine prolonged median overall survival by over nine months compared to standard of care in a Phase 3 trial for difficult-to-treat acute myeloid leukemia.

title: Lilly pens another deal, inking up to $5.9B oncology pact with Stipple
snippet: A licensing pact with Stipple Bio was one of two announced by Eli Lilly on Monday, after the up to $1.5 billion buyout of blood cancer-focused Calytrix Bio.

title: Genetix’s genetic medicines are officially profitable, with $327M in sales YTD
snippet: It’s been a long road to financial stability for Genetix Biotherapeutics, the rebranded name of bluebird bio following its February 2025 sale to two private equity firms, but on Monday the biotech estimated full year 2026 sales will reach $500 million.

title: Marrow Therapeutics debuts with $173M to tackle blood disorders in vivo
snippet: Marrow Therapeutics aims to address safety and accessibility obstacles in genetic medicines by delivering therapies straight to bone marrow cells.

title: Biotech’s boardroom gains for women fail to translate to CEO roles
snippet: Women held 29% of biotech board seats in fiscal year 2025 but just 8.8% of CEO roles, highlighting uneven progress across industry leadership spots.

title: Serious adverse events mar robust efficacy data for Helus’ psychedelic in major depression
snippet: Helus Pharma's psilocin-based HLP003 significantly reduced symptoms of major depressive disorder in the adjuvant setting in a Phase 3 trial but was tripped up in the stock market by three serious adverse events.

title: J&J pays $2.2B upfront for Ollin, taps Blackstone to fund eye disease trial
snippet: Blackstone will provide $750 million for Phase 3 development of Ollin Biosciences’ retinal disease bispecific as Johnson & Johnson looks to bolster its eye therapeutics pipeline after several setbacks.

title: Lilly’s early-stage M&A quest finds $1.5B deal for Calytrix’s blood cancer work
snippet: Eli Lilly's business development team has inked 14 buyouts this year so far, with Calytrix Bio tucking into the pharma’s oncology pipeline.

title: FDA’s Summit rejection puts PD-1xVEGF class on notice to establish overall survival
snippet: The FDA rejected Summit Therapeutics’ ivonescimab over the weekend, sending a strong message to rival drugmakers Bristol Myers Squibb, BioNTech, Pfizer, Merck and AbbVie.

title: Novo’s CagriSema drives more than 20% weight loss at lower doses
snippet: As Novo awaits an FDA decision for its next-gen obesity asset, the company has presented more data at ObesityWeek that could help buoy sentiment on the amylin/GLP-1 combination that disappointed investors a couple of years ago.

title: Their loss, our gain? Canada makes its case to Europe amid U.S. instability
snippet: Companies at BIO-Europe said shifting U.S. politics have created an opening to promote Canada’s strengths to European partners.

title: ObesityWeek 2026: Wave outlines case for body composition–based trial design
snippet: Across three cohorts in Wave Life Sciences’ mid-stage trial of WVE-007, higher baseline body mass index and excessive body fat have been associated with a more pronounced effect, Rodman & Renshaw said following the company’s ObesityWeek update.

title: Rising costs leave 9 in 10 new medicines unprofitable, IQVIA finds
snippet: To achieve a positive return, drugs launched from 2016 to 2020 must generate nearly $12 billion in sales, up from just $1.4 billion for drugs launched in the early 1990s.

title: Seawolf surfaces with $100M, $1.2B Sanofi pact for redosable DNA medicines
snippet: Backed by Novartis’ venture arm, Eli Lilly and CRISPR Therapeutics, Seawolf is advancing its nonviral DNA delivery platform while inking a pact with Sanofi.

title: Emerging biotech hubs step up as innovation economics evolve
snippet: How India and other emerging hubs for drug development can be key to reshaping medical costs globally.

title: BioSpace 40 Under 40 winners Paull, Zhang let patients with rare disease lead the way at BridgeBio
snippet: BridgeBio has produced two young leaders on BioSpace’s 2026 40 Under 40 list. Morgan Paull and Christine Zhang attribute their early success to the company’s unique hub-and-spoke model and a drive to help patients with few treatment options. “It’s very personal,” Paull said.

title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
